# Purpose

This analysis addresses the revision-plan request for an **illustrative outcomes-averted-per-dose
sensitivity analysis**.

It compares the same municipality prioritization rules already used in File 13:

1. transmission-only;
2. age/severity-only;
3. expected-burden.

All rules select the same top one-third of Brazil's 5,570 municipalities (`n = 1,857`).

The calculation is restricted to the **18-59-year population**, matching the current Brazilian
age window used elsewhere in the revision. It uses the primary model's fitted 2024-2025
municipality-month incidence surface together with the same age-specific observed CFR weights
used in File 13.

This is **not a vaccine impact evaluation**. It is a transparent scenario calculation under
assumed direct vaccine efficacy and coverage. It does not model indirect protection, transmission
feedback, waning, implementation constraints, or causal vaccine effectiveness.

A useful mathematical consequence is made explicit: under this linear direct-protection model,
coverage changes the **total number of outcomes averted**, but not the expected number averted
per 1,000 administered doses. The code verifies this rather than hiding it.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(purrr)
})

EXPECTED_N_MUNI <- 5570L
TOP_N <- ceiling(EXPECTED_N_MUNI / 3)

STUDY_YEARS <- 2024:2025

# Illustrative scenario values from the revision-plan logic.
# These are assumptions, not empirical VE or coverage estimates.
EFFICACY_GRID <- c(0.50, 0.70, 0.90)
COVERAGE_GRID <- c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75)

# Equal-dose national supply scenarios used for the head-to-head comparison.
# Each value is the fraction of the national 18-59 eligible population for
# which one dose is available. Every prioritization rule receives exactly
# the same dose budget in a given scenario.
DOSE_BUDGET_FRAC_GRID <- c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75)

# Monte Carlo draws for uncertainty in the observed age-specific CFR weights.
# Jeffreys beta posterior is used only as a sensitivity device.
N_DRAWS <- 2000L
SEED <- 20261003L

RESULT_ROOT <- path.expand("~/Downloads/inla_results")
OUT_DIR <- file.path(RESULT_ROOT, "averted_burden_sensitivity")
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ST_RATE_PATH <- file.path(
  RESULT_ROOT,
  "st_rate_chik_region_2016_2025.rds"
)

PRIORITY_PATH <- file.path(
  RESULT_ROOT,
  "priority_rule_evaluation_municipality_2024_2025.csv"
)

POP_AGE_PATH <- path.expand("~/pop_panel_age.rds")

required_files <- c(
  ST_RATE_PATH,
  PRIORITY_PATH,
  POP_AGE_PATH
)

missing_files <- required_files[!file.exists(required_files)]

if (length(missing_files) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Required saved inputs are missing:\n",
    paste(missing_files, collapse = "\n")
  )
}

if (!exists("Chik_total")) {
  stop(
    "Chik_total is not currently in memory. Run 01_data_import_cleaning.Rmd once in this ",
    "R session, then rerun File 20. No INLA refit is required."
  )
}

cat("Municipalities:", EXPECTED_N_MUNI, "\n")
cat("Matched top-third:", TOP_N, "\n")
cat("Efficacy scenarios:", paste(EFFICACY_GRID, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Coverage scenarios:", paste(COVERAGE_GRID, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# 1. Load saved model and priority outputs

```{r load-inputs}
st_rate <- readRDS(ST_RATE_PATH) %>%
  mutate(
    ym_date = as.Date(ym_date),
    year = lubridate::year(ym_date),
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(year %in% STUDY_YEARS)

priority <- readr::read_csv(
  PRIORITY_PATH,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(
    code_muni = col_character(),
    .default = col_guess()
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  )

pop_panel_age <- readRDS(POP_AGE_PATH) %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    ),
    year = as.integer(year)
  )

required_priority_cols <- c(
  "code_muni", "T_irr", "V_burden", "combined_burden"
)

stopifnot(
  all(required_priority_cols %in% names(priority)),
  nrow(priority) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  dplyr::n_distinct(priority$code_muni) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  all(c("code_muni", "ym_date", "year", "rate_per_person") %in% names(st_rate)),
  dplyr::n_distinct(st_rate$code_muni) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI
)

cat("2024-2025 fitted-rate rows:", nrow(st_rate), "\n")
```

# 2. Recreate the age-specific fatality weights used in File 13

Six age bands are reconstructed exactly as in File 13. The dose-averted calculation itself uses
only the licensed 18-59 age window (`18-39` and `40-59`).

```{r cfr-weights}
decode_age_years <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  unit_code <- floor(x / 1000)
  value <- x %% 1000

  dplyr::case_when(
    unit_code == 1 ~ value / (24 * 365),
    unit_code == 2 ~ value / 365,
    unit_code == 3 ~ value / 12,
    unit_code == 4 ~ value,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
}

chik_severity <- Chik_total %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)),
    age_years = decode_age_years(NU_IDADE_N),
    age_band = case_when(
      !is.na(age_years) & age_years < 18 ~ "0-17",
      age_years >= 18 & age_years < 40 ~ "18-39",
      age_years >= 40 & age_years < 60 ~ "40-59",
      age_years >= 60 & age_years < 70 ~ "60-69",
      age_years >= 70 & age_years < 80 ~ "70-79",
      age_years >= 80 ~ "80+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    death = as.integer(as.character(EVOLUCAO) == "2")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    year %in% 2016:2025,
    CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13),
    !is.na(age_band)
  )

cfr_weights <- chik_severity %>%
  group_by(age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    cases = n(),
    deaths = sum(death, na.rm = TRUE),
    CFR = deaths / cases,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(cfr_weights)

eligible_cfr <- cfr_weights %>%
  filter(age_band %in% c("18-39", "40-59"))

stopifnot(
  nrow(eligible_cfr) == 2L,
  all(eligible_cfr$cases > 0L),
  all(eligible_cfr$deaths >= 0L)
)
```

# 3. Build municipality-year eligible population

```{r eligible-population}
eligible_pop_year <- pop_panel_age %>%
  filter(
    year %in% STUDY_YEARS,
    age >= 18,
    age < 60
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    age_band = case_when(
      age >= 18 & age < 40 ~ "18-39",
      age >= 40 & age < 60 ~ "40-59",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year, age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

eligible_pop_mean <- eligible_pop_year %>%
  group_by(code_muni, year) %>%
  summarise(
    eligible_pop_year = sum(pop),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    eligible_pop = mean(eligible_pop_year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(eligible_pop_mean) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  all(is.finite(eligible_pop_mean$eligible_pop)),
  all(eligible_pop_mean$eligible_pop > 0)
)
```

# 4. Absolute fitted 2024-2025 burden in the eligible age window

The primary INLA output already contains an absolute fitted municipality-month incidence
(`rate_per_person = fitted cases / municipality population`).

For each municipality-month, age-specific expected cases are approximated by applying that
municipality's fitted incidence to the corresponding age-specific population. This assumes the
within-municipality infection incidence is proportional across eligible age bands.

Expected deaths are then obtained by applying the observed age-specific CFR weights.

```{r expected-eligible-burden}
eligible_monthly <- st_rate %>%
  select(
    code_muni,
    ym_date,
    year,
    rate_per_person
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    eligible_pop_year,
    by = c("code_muni", "year"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    eligible_cfr %>%
      select(age_band, CFR),
    by = "age_band"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_cases_age = rate_per_person * pop,
    expected_deaths_age = expected_cases_age * CFR
  )

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(eligible_monthly$pop),
  !anyNA(eligible_monthly$CFR),
  all(is.finite(eligible_monthly$expected_cases_age)),
  all(is.finite(eligible_monthly$expected_deaths_age))
)

eligible_burden_muni <- eligible_monthly %>%
  group_by(code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    expected_cases_eligible_2425 =
      sum(expected_cases_age, na.rm = TRUE),
    expected_deaths_eligible_2425 =
      sum(expected_deaths_age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    eligible_pop_mean,
    by = "code_muni"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(eligible_burden_muni) == EXPECTED_N_MUNI,
  all(is.finite(eligible_burden_muni$expected_cases_eligible_2425)),
  all(is.finite(eligible_burden_muni$expected_deaths_eligible_2425))
)

cat(
  "Model-implied eligible-age cases, 2024-2025:",
  sum(eligible_burden_muni$expected_cases_eligible_2425), "\n"
)

cat(
  "Model-implied eligible-age deaths, 2024-2025:",
  sum(eligible_burden_muni$expected_deaths_eligible_2425), "\n"
)
```

# 5. Define matched-coverage prioritization rules

```{r ranking-rules}
rule_specs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~rule, ~score_col,
  "Transmission-only", "T_irr",
  "Age/severity-only", "V_burden",
  "Expected-burden", "combined_burden"
)

analysis_muni <- priority %>%
  select(
    code_muni,
    T_irr,
    V_burden,
    combined_burden
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    eligible_burden_muni,
    by = "code_muni"
  )

select_rule <- function(dat, score_col, rule_name) {
  dat %>%
    arrange(
      desc(.data[[score_col]]),
      code_muni
    ) %>%
    slice_head(n = TOP_N) %>%
    mutate(rule = rule_name)
}

selected_by_rule <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  rule_specs$score_col,
  rule_specs$rule,
  ~ select_rule(analysis_muni, .x, .y)
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    selected_by_rule %>%
      count(rule) %>%
      pull(n) == TOP_N
  )
)
```

# 6. Deterministic efficacy × coverage scenario grid

For each selected municipality set:

- `doses = coverage × eligible population`;
- `cases averted = efficacy × coverage × expected eligible-age cases`;
- `deaths averted = efficacy × coverage × expected eligible-age deaths`.

This is a deliberately simple direct-protection calculation.

```{r deterministic-grid}
rule_burden <- selected_by_rule %>%
  group_by(rule) %>%
  summarise(
    selected_eligible_pop =
      sum(eligible_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    expected_cases_eligible_2425 =
      sum(expected_cases_eligible_2425, na.rm = TRUE),
    expected_deaths_eligible_2425 =
      sum(expected_deaths_eligible_2425, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

scenario_grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  efficacy = EFFICACY_GRID,
  coverage = COVERAGE_GRID
)

averted_scenarios <- tidyr::crossing(
  rule = rule_burden$rule,
  efficacy = EFFICACY_GRID,
  coverage = COVERAGE_GRID
) %>%
  left_join(
    rule_burden,
    by = "rule"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    doses_administered =
      coverage * selected_eligible_pop,

    expected_cases_averted =
      efficacy * coverage *
      expected_cases_eligible_2425,

    expected_deaths_averted =
      efficacy * coverage *
      expected_deaths_eligible_2425,

    cases_averted_per_1000_doses =
      1000 * expected_cases_averted /
      doses_administered,

    deaths_averted_per_1000_doses =
      1000 * expected_deaths_averted /
      doses_administered
  )

print(averted_scenarios)
```


# 6A. Equal-dose national supply comparison

The coverage-based calculation above applies the same percentage coverage within each
rule's selected municipalities. Because the selected eligible populations differ by rule,
that design does **not** hold the number of administered doses fixed.

Reviewer 2's "outcomes averted per dose" question is therefore also evaluated under an
equal-dose constraint. In each national supply scenario, every prioritization rule receives
the same total dose budget. Municipalities are traversed from highest to lowest priority
score, with full coverage within each municipality until the remaining budget is smaller
than the next municipality's eligible population; the boundary municipality then receives
partial coverage. This is an illustrative greedy allocation, not an operational optimization
that incorporates delivery costs, uptake, contraindications, or dose wastage.

```{r fixed-dose-budget-allocation}
national_eligible_pop <- sum(
  analysis_muni$eligible_pop,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

dose_budget_grid <- tibble::tibble(
  dose_budget_fraction = DOSE_BUDGET_FRAC_GRID,
  dose_budget = national_eligible_pop *
    DOSE_BUDGET_FRAC_GRID
)

allocate_fixed_doses <- function(
  dat,
  score_col,
  rule_name,
  dose_budget
) {

  ranked <- dat %>%
    arrange(
      desc(.data[[score_col]]),
      code_muni
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      cumulative_eligible_pop =
        cumsum(eligible_pop),
      cumulative_eligible_pop_before =
        cumulative_eligible_pop -
        eligible_pop,
      allocated_doses =
        pmax(
          0,
          pmin(
            eligible_pop,
            dose_budget -
              cumulative_eligible_pop_before
          )
        ),
      allocated_coverage =
        dplyr::if_else(
          eligible_pop > 0,
          allocated_doses / eligible_pop,
          0
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(allocated_doses > 0) %>%
    mutate(
      rule = rule_name,
      dose_budget = dose_budget
    )

  allocated_total <- sum(
    ranked$allocated_doses,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  stopifnot(
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        allocated_total,
        min(
          dose_budget,
          national_eligible_pop
        ),
        tolerance = 1e-6
      )
    )
  )

  ranked
}

fixed_dose_allocations <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  tidyr::crossing(
    rule = rule_specs$rule,
    dose_budget_fraction =
      DOSE_BUDGET_FRAC_GRID
  ) %>%
    left_join(
      rule_specs,
      by = "rule"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      dose_budget =
        national_eligible_pop *
        dose_budget_fraction
    ),
  function(
    rule,
    dose_budget_fraction,
    score_col,
    dose_budget
  ) {
    allocate_fixed_doses(
      dat = analysis_muni,
      score_col = score_col,
      rule_name = rule,
      dose_budget = dose_budget
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        dose_budget_fraction =
          dose_budget_fraction
      )
  }
)

fixed_dose_rule_totals <-
  fixed_dose_allocations %>%
  group_by(
    rule,
    dose_budget_fraction,
    dose_budget
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    doses_administered =
      sum(allocated_doses),
    municipalities_reached =
      n(),
    fully_covered_municipalities =
      sum(
        allocated_coverage >=
          1 - 1e-12
      ),
    boundary_coverage =
      min(
        allocated_coverage,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    expected_cases_exposed =
      sum(
        allocated_coverage *
          expected_cases_eligible_2425,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    expected_deaths_exposed =
      sum(
        allocated_coverage *
          expected_deaths_eligible_2425,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(fixed_dose_rule_totals)
```

# 6B. Equal-dose efficacy scenarios

Because the total number of administered doses is identical across rules within each
dose-budget scenario, differences in outcomes averted are directly attributable to where
the doses are allocated under the model assumptions.

```{r fixed-dose-efficacy-grid}
fixed_dose_scenarios <-
  tidyr::crossing(
    rule = rule_specs$rule,
    dose_budget_fraction =
      DOSE_BUDGET_FRAC_GRID,
    efficacy = EFFICACY_GRID
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    fixed_dose_rule_totals,
    by = c(
      "rule",
      "dose_budget_fraction"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_cases_averted =
      efficacy *
      expected_cases_exposed,

    expected_deaths_averted =
      efficacy *
      expected_deaths_exposed,

    cases_averted_per_1000_doses =
      1000 *
      expected_cases_averted /
      doses_administered,

    deaths_averted_per_1000_doses =
      1000 *
      expected_deaths_averted /
      doses_administered
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    dose_budget_fraction,
    efficacy,
    desc(
      deaths_averted_per_1000_doses
    )
  )

print(fixed_dose_scenarios)

fixed_dose_equal_budget_check <-
  fixed_dose_scenarios %>%
  group_by(
    dose_budget_fraction,
    efficacy
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    min_doses =
      min(doses_administered),
    max_doses =
      max(doses_administered),
    dose_difference =
      max_doses - min_doses,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(fixed_dose_equal_budget_check)

stopifnot(
  max(
    fixed_dose_equal_budget_check$
      dose_difference
  ) < 1e-6
)
```

# 6C. Compact fixed-dose comparison at VE = 0.70

This table is the most direct answer to the limited-supply question. It compares all three
rules at exactly the same national dose budget.

```{r fixed-dose-compact-70}
fixed_dose_compact_70 <-
  fixed_dose_scenarios %>%
  filter(
    abs(efficacy - 0.70) < 1e-12
  ) %>%
  select(
    rule,
    dose_budget_fraction,
    doses_administered,
    municipalities_reached,
    fully_covered_municipalities,
    expected_cases_averted,
    expected_deaths_averted,
    cases_averted_per_1000_doses,
    deaths_averted_per_1000_doses
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    dose_budget_fraction,
    desc(
      deaths_averted_per_1000_doses
    )
  )

print(fixed_dose_compact_70)
```

# 6E. CFR uncertainty under the equal-dose design

The equal-dose comparison above uses point estimates of the age-specific CFR. To match
Reviewer 2's request for uncertainty, we repeat the fixed-dose calculation over the same
Jeffreys-posterior CFR draws used elsewhere in this file.

The ranking and the dose allocation are held fixed within each rule. Thus these intervals
represent uncertainty in the age-specific CFR weights conditional on the fitted incidence
surface and on the selected ranking, rather than full posterior uncertainty in the ranking
itself.

```{r fixed-dose-cfr-uncertainty}
# Reuse the same age-specific CFR draws if they have already been created later
# in an interactive session; otherwise create them here.
if (!exists("cfr_draws")) {
  set.seed(SEED)

  cfr_draws <- eligible_cfr %>%
    mutate(
      draw = purrr::map2(
        deaths,
        cases,
        ~ stats::rbeta(
          N_DRAWS,
          shape1 = .x + 0.5,
          shape2 = (.y - .x) + 0.5
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    select(age_band, draw) %>%
    tidyr::unnest_longer(
      draw,
      indices_to = "draw_id"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      draw_id = as.integer(draw_id)
    )
}

if (!exists("burden_by_muni_age")) {
  burden_by_muni_age <- eligible_monthly %>%
    group_by(
      code_muni,
      age_band
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      expected_cases_age_2425 =
        sum(
          expected_cases_age,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

fixed_dose_age_burden <-
  fixed_dose_allocations %>%
  select(
    rule,
    dose_budget_fraction,
    code_muni,
    allocated_doses,
    allocated_coverage
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    burden_by_muni_age,
    by = "code_muni",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_cases_age_exposed =
      allocated_coverage *
      expected_cases_age_2425
  )

fixed_dose_draw_deaths <-
  fixed_dose_age_burden %>%
  inner_join(
    cfr_draws,
    by = "age_band",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_deaths_draw =
      expected_cases_age_exposed *
      draw
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    rule,
    dose_budget_fraction,
    draw_id
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    expected_deaths_exposed =
      sum(
        expected_deaths_draw,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    fixed_dose_rule_totals %>%
      select(
        rule,
        dose_budget_fraction,
        doses_administered
      ),
    by = c(
      "rule",
      "dose_budget_fraction"
    )
  )

fixed_dose_uncertainty <-
  tidyr::crossing(
    efficacy = EFFICACY_GRID
  ) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    fixed_dose_draw_deaths
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_deaths_averted =
      efficacy *
      expected_deaths_exposed,

    deaths_averted_per_1000_doses =
      1000 *
      expected_deaths_averted /
      doses_administered
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    rule,
    dose_budget_fraction,
    efficacy
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    deaths_averted_median =
      median(
        expected_deaths_averted
      ),
    deaths_averted_lo =
      quantile(
        expected_deaths_averted,
        0.025
      ),
    deaths_averted_hi =
      quantile(
        expected_deaths_averted,
        0.975
      ),
    deaths_per_1000_median =
      median(
        deaths_averted_per_1000_doses
      ),
    deaths_per_1000_lo =
      quantile(
        deaths_averted_per_1000_doses,

      ),
    deaths_per_1000_hi =
      quantile(
        deaths_averted_per_1000_doses,
        0.975
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(

  n = Inf
)
```

# 7. Verify the coverage-cancellation property

Under a linear direct-protection model, per-dose efficiency should be identical across coverage
values for a fixed efficacy and prioritization rule.

```{r coverage-invariance}
coverage_invariance <- averted_scenarios %>%
  group_by(rule, efficacy) %>%
  summarise(
    min_deaths_per_1000 =
      min(deaths_averted_per_1000_doses),
    max_deaths_per_1000 =
      max(deaths_averted_per_1000_doses),
    range_deaths_per_1000 =
      max_deaths_per_1000 - min_deaths_per_1000,

    min_cases_per_1000 =
      min(cases_averted_per_1000_doses),
    max_cases_per_1000 =
      max(cases_averted_per_1000_doses),
    range_cases_per_1000 =
      max_cases_per_1000 - min_cases_per_1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(coverage_invariance)

stopifnot(
  max(coverage_invariance$range_deaths_per_1000) < 1e-10,
  max(coverage_invariance$range_cases_per_1000) < 1e-10
)
```

# 8. CFR uncertainty sensitivity

This section propagates uncertainty in the two eligible-age observed CFR weights using independent
Jeffreys beta posteriors:

`CFR_a ~ Beta(deaths_a + 0.5, cases_a - deaths_a + 0.5)`.

This does **not** represent full model posterior uncertainty. In particular, covariance in the INLA
fitted incidence surface is not propagated. The primary INLA fit used `control.compute` without
`config = TRUE` and with `return.marginals = FALSE`, so valid joint latent-field posterior sampling
cannot be reconstructed from the saved fit without refitting the primary model. We therefore do
not manufacture pseudo-posterior draws from marginal standard deviations. The resulting interval
is labeled as a **CFR-uncertainty sensitivity interval**, not a full posterior credible interval.

```{r cfr-uncertainty}
set.seed(SEED)

cfr_draws <- eligible_cfr %>%
  mutate(
    draw = purrr::map2(
      deaths,
      cases,
      ~ stats::rbeta(
        N_DRAWS,
        shape1 = .x + 0.5,
        shape2 = (.y - .x) + 0.5
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(age_band, draw) %>%
  tidyr::unnest_longer(draw, indices_to = "draw_id") %>%
  mutate(draw_id = as.integer(draw_id))

# Aggregate the fitted 2024-2025 case burden by municipality and eligible age band.
burden_by_muni_age <- eligible_monthly %>%
  group_by(code_muni, age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    expected_cases_age_2425 =
      sum(expected_cases_age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

selected_codes <- selected_by_rule %>%
  select(rule, code_muni)

selected_age_burden <- selected_codes %>%
  left_join(
    burden_by_muni_age,
    by = "code_muni",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  group_by(rule, age_band) %>%
  summarise(
    expected_cases_age_2425 =
      sum(expected_cases_age_2425),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

draw_rule_deaths <- selected_age_burden %>%
  inner_join(
    cfr_draws,
    by = "age_band",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_deaths_draw =
      expected_cases_age_2425 * draw
  ) %>%
  group_by(rule, draw_id) %>%
  summarise(
    expected_deaths_eligible_2425 =
      sum(expected_deaths_draw),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    rule_burden %>%
      select(rule, selected_eligible_pop),
    by = "rule"
  )

deaths_per_1000_uncertainty <- tidyr::crossing(
  efficacy = EFFICACY_GRID,
  coverage = COVERAGE_GRID
) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    draw_rule_deaths
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    doses_administered =
      coverage * selected_eligible_pop,

    expected_deaths_averted =
      efficacy * coverage *
      expected_deaths_eligible_2425,

    deaths_averted_per_1000_doses =
      1000 * expected_deaths_averted /
      doses_administered
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    rule,
    efficacy,
    coverage
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    deaths_per_1000_median =
      median(deaths_averted_per_1000_doses),
    deaths_per_1000_lo =
      quantile(
        deaths_averted_per_1000_doses,
        0.025
      ),
    deaths_per_1000_hi =
      quantile(
        deaths_averted_per_1000_doses,
        0.975
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(deaths_per_1000_uncertainty)
```

# Interpretation guardrails

- This is an **illustrative scenario calculation**, not a causal vaccine impact analysis.
- The assumed efficacy values (0.50, 0.70, 0.90) and coverage values (0.25, 0.50, 0.75)
  are sensitivity scenarios, not empirical estimates.
- The calculation assumes direct protection is linear in coverage and efficacy.
- It assumes the primary model's municipality-specific incidence applies proportionally to the
  eligible 18-59 age bands within each municipality.
- It does not model indirect effects, herd protection, waning, dose wastage, contraindications
  beyond age, logistics, or behavioral responses.
- Because this is a linear direct-protection model, coverage changes total expected burden
  averted but **does not change outcomes averted per 1,000 administered doses**.
- The reported uncertainty interval propagates uncertainty in the age-specific CFR weights only.
  It is **not a full posterior credible interval** for the vaccine impact calculation.
- The purpose is to compare prioritization rules under common assumptions, not to estimate the
  real-world effect of the 2026 pilot.
